title: Buying a grocery store for security after reading Dan Burley's column
summary: Having read of musicians ending up broke, he bought a grocery store in the Bronx for security.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: You had a lovely home up there -- where was that?
In the Bronx.
In the Bronx. Yeah, I remember going up there; it was a lovely place. And you also had a grocery store there once, didn't you?
Yeah, I called myself -- trying to get some security.
A tycoon!

Yeah. Tried to get a little bit of security, because you know, there was one thing that always bothered me. When I first came to New York and I saw all these musicians that I used to hear about -- at that time, this was before DownBeat, so I used to read about them in the Pittsburgh Courier, which was a black newspaper, and there
was a guy who wrote for it named Dan Burley who used to write about all of the musicians and the entertainment around town in the Pittsburgh Courier.
Did he write for the Courier or the Defender?
No, he wrote for the ...
Because I went to school with Dan Burley.
He had a column in the Pittsburgh Courier.
I'm sure he first wrote for the Defender, because he was a skillful piano player.
That's right, that's right.
Well, I knew him in high school.
Well, he played -- I think he wrote for the Defender first and then he was writing ...
He came to New York here. He was in New York.

Yeah, and he had a column that -- I think it was Dan Burley that wrote this column in the Pittsburgh Courier, and they used to have, like, during those days, they used to have, like all of the band, the routes, where they were going, and they had a writeup about all of the different musicians and the entertainers and that.
So when I came to New York and I saw these people that I used to read about and saw the position that they

were in, because they were taking their money and spending it up across the bars and things, and not looking out for what's gonna happen tomorrow, I said to myself, 'Well, I don't want to be like that when I get so that I can't play -- I want to be in a position where I would be able to still take care of myself.'
So that was one reason why I bought that grocery store -- that was for security.
I remember how happy you were then -- you used to tell me how much beer you used to sell on Sunday -- that was a nice thing.
Yeah, well that was the reason for that. I did not want to end up like a lot of musicians that I had read about.
